ud1.6:1.2: at one time the Fortunate One was dwelling near Rājagaha, in Bamboo Wood, at the Squirrels’ Feeding Place.
ud1.6:1.3: Then at that time venerable Mahākassapa was dwelling in the Pepper Cave, and was afflicted, suffering, and very sick.
ud1.6:1.4: Then venerable Mahākassapa at another time arose from that affliction.
ud1.6:1.5: Then this occurred to venerable Mahākassapa when he arose from that affliction:
ud1.6:1.6: “Well now, I should enter Rājagaha for alms.”
ud1.6:2.1: Then at that time five hundred devatās were ready and eager to offer almsfood to venerable Mahākassapa.
ud1.6:2.2: But venerable Mahākassapa, after refusing those five hundred devatās, having dressed in the morning time, after picking up his bowl and robe, entered Rājagaha for alms,
ud1.6:2.3: (going) to the poor streets, to the wretched streets, to the weaver’s streets.
ud1.6:2.4: The Fortunate One saw venerable Mahākassapa walking for alms in Rājagaha, (going) to the poor streets, to the wretched streets, to the weaver’s streets.
ud1.6:3.1: Then the Fortunate One, having understood the significance of it, on that occasion uttered this exalted utterance:
ud1.6:4.1: “Not nourishing another, well-known, controlled, established in the essential,
ud1.6:4.3: With pollutants destroyed, rid of faults: him I call a brāhmaṇa.”
